Ransomware Attack Disrupts Zimbabwe Aerospace & Defense Firms

A ransomware attack targeting Zimbabwe's Aerospace & Defense sector has caused significant disruption across several companies, with operations at key manufacturing sites and research facilities currently halted. The attack, which began early Tuesday morning, has encrypted critical IT systems, forcing firms to suspend production lines and restrict employee access to secure data.

Among the hardest hit is ZimAero Dynamics, one of the country’s largest defense contractors. The company confirmed that its main facility in Harare has been offline since the attack began. “All our technical and administrative staff have been instructed to remain on standby while our cybersecurity teams work to restore access,” said a spokesperson for ZimAero Dynamics. “We are prioritizing the protection of sensitive project information and the safety of our workforce.”

Other firms, including Skyward Technologies and Harare Aeronautics, have also reported system outages and delays. Workers at these sites have been sent home or reassigned to non-digital tasks, with union representatives expressing concern over the potential duration of the disruption. “Many of our members rely on consistent work schedules, and the uncertainty caused by this incident is deeply worrying,” said Tendai Moyo, chairperson of the Aerospace & Defense Workers Union.

Industry analysts estimate that up to 70% of the sector’s output capacity is currently affected. The Zimbabwe Aerospace & Defense Industry Council issued a statement urging all firms to review their cybersecurity protocols and cooperate fully with ongoing investigations. “This event underscores the strategic importance of robust digital defenses in our sector,” said council president Douglas Chikore.

As of Wednesday afternoon, negotiations with the attackers are ongoing, and no timeline for full recovery has been provided. Authorities have not disclosed whether any sensitive defense data has been compromised, but investigations are active and ongoing.
